claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Original enrollment was 26, with one response-recording failure and five additional fMRI error-rate exclusions, leaving 20 final modeled fMRI participants.
Task stimuli are digits 1-9 excluding 5; an 80 percent one-digit upper parity baseline and remaining two-digit critical trial class with brightness-dependent instruction.
Baseline asks upper-stimulus odd/even; distractor keeps parity rule under stronger upper cue, switch moves to lower brighter digit magnitude greater/less than five.

Original human trials each last 2 seconds with 900 ms visual stimulus and response throughout; pseudorandomized experimental schedule includes between 3 and 6 baseline trials after each critical trial, including collected ambiguous critical trials. The ambiguous trials are NOT among those simulated by the fixed neural model.

Ambiguous-condition trials were collected but excluded from explicit neural model because cue lacks unambiguous correct answer, was untrained and may recruit learning/higher control; handled in fMRI separately.

Original task uses fixed synaptic strengths and already trained parity/magnitude rules. Before scanning, training lasted approximately 25 min: single tasks individually trained to at least 90 percent correct, then combined task without ambiguity trained to 80 percent correct separately for baseline, switch, distractor. The modeled short scanner task is NOT new learning.
Integrated architecture contains distinct rule-representing working-memory module and four-choice decision module with top-down rule-to-decision synaptic projection and bottom-up stimulus input.
Authors explicitly adapt Stemme 2005 integrated task-switching network; reductions additionally use Wong/Wang 2006 rule dynamics and extend Roxin/Ledberg 2008 two-choice decision reduction.
Rule circuit comprises two strongly recurrent rule-selective pyramidal pools, shared inhibitory and nonselective populations; competition yields a spontaneous state and two high-rule attractors.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF Fig3 pp5-7, Methods pp27-30 Eq1-2

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Reduced rule state uses synaptic gating vector S=(S1,S2) with rates r1,r2 determined by effective nonlinear transfer functions and physiological scaling connections.
Rule-specific external currents encode relative brightness to bias the competing rule populations; current task rule persists under sufficient attractor stability.
Finite-size rule noise modeled by OU variables added directly to synaptic gating dynamics rather than presynaptic currents as in Wong/Wang; p30 Eq3-4.
Full generic decision ancestor is five rate populations: four choice-selective excitatory units and one shared inhibitory population with recurrent excitation and feedback inhibition.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF Fig3A p6, Methods pp30-31 Eq5

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: At near-bifurcation loss of spontaneous-state stability, three zero-eigenvalue modes of five-population linearization give 3D reduced variables X,Y,Z; remaining modes decay.
Four selective choice growth directions embed as corners of symmetric tetrahedron around reduced spontaneous origin; quadratic nonlinear terms yield winner-take-all diverging trajectories.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF Fig3 pp6-9, Methods pp31-34 Eq6-8

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Decision forcing is sum of rule population top-down rates r1/r2 weighted c_plus and bottom-up stimulus input Dij for correct/wrong feature under parity/magnitude; four separate choice channels.
Reduced decision evolution adds OU-type stochastic noise to X,Y,Z and is written as three coupled nonlinear drift terms in Eq7-8; exact p33 printed noise-time coefficient is excluded.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF p33 printed OU expression and Eq7, p34 Eq8; PRE_A_MATH_ADJUDICATION

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Decision readout projects reduced X,Y,Z onto all four choice directions and registers the first projection crossing an IMPLEMENTED 10 Hz threshold. Nonlinear divergence implies weak threshold sensitivity only for thresholds sufficiently far from the spontaneous origin, not a fixed biological threshold universally.
Each simulated trial initializes rule to parity high attractor and decision to X=Y=Z=0; rules propagate 900 ms with input followed by 1100 ms with input removed.

All 20 analyzed individuals had subject-specific fits of choice frequencies and response-time distributions across modeled baseline/distractor/switch; this is fit to observed behavior, not out-of-sample prediction.

Per-subject behavioral fitting simulated 1024 trials per modeled condition. The likelihood combined multinomial choice and two-sample KS conditional RT distributions under Gaussian parameter priors. Metropolis-Hastings used TWO 1,000,000-step chains with Gaussian proposal sigma_MH=0.01; 50,000 burn-in steps discarded per chain, chains pooled, locally adaptive KDE used for MAP. No held-out predictive test was done.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF pp35-37 Bayesian posterior and MAP

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Paper reports 10 of 300 goodness-of-fit tests significant at conventional 0.05 with many high p values; failure to reject is not proof of model identity or independent generalization.
Behavior-fitted model's condition/choice-dependent rule-module sum-spike-rate integral is normalized, aligned to individual trial logs, z-scaled and convolved with canonical HRF as BOLD regressor.

Two distinct fMRI GLMs must be separated. For model-derived rule-module BOLD prediction, each individual ambiguous trial receives its own nuisance regressor plus six motion regressors (p40). For the independent switch-minus-distractor contrast, ambiguous trials are collapsed into switched/stayed regressors plus one error regressor and six motion, with normal baseline trials implicit (p41). Explicit neural simulation excludes ambiguous trials.

Rule-module BOLD regressor statistically associates with IFJ and IPS activation plus weaker other foci at stated group-corrected thresholds; this localization does not prove unique physical implementation.
For source-defined rule dynamics, numerical Fokker-Planck stationary probability Pss over (S1,S2) defines generalized U=-ln Pss, conditioned by fitted NMDA/GABA/noise parameters.
Rule dynamics are nonconservative and can retain nonzero divergence-free steady current Jss; U captures stationary density only, not a classical conservative energy nor all directional path dynamics.

The individually fitted sigma_rule noise parameters were multiplied by 10 solely for illustrating Fig7, which includes generalized potential landscapes, dominant transition paths and potential profiles. The original model fits, other figures and empirically measured activation are NOT claimed to be multiplied by 10.

Source-defined directional physiology: increased sNMDA recurrent excitation stabilizes/deepens active high-rule basins; increased sGABA inhibitory conductance destabilizes high-rule activity while stabilizing the spontaneous low-activity basin; greater sigma_rule diffusion smoothes generalized U and facilitates transitions. These combine in individually fitted models; nearby Table2 behavioral trends do not survive corrected significance testing.

Reported participant minimal action is the DIRECTIONAL rule1(parity)-to-rule2(magnitude) optimal transition between active rule attractors; source numerical choices E_eff=-V(S_min) for longest kinetic time, 50 discretized line elements, penalty 10^5 on variance of element length, MATLAB fminunc minimization. Fig7 plots forward and reverse illustrative paths, which need not be symmetric.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF pp14,17,39 Estimation of Minimal Action

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Model minimal action is associated with the observed switch-minus-distractor brain response in TWO separate corrected scopes: left middle frontal gyrus under whole-brain FWE-corrected cluster threshold, and thalamostriatal group under separate anatomically defined bilateral thalamus/caudate ROI FWE-corrected threshold. ROI association is NOT a whole-brain corrected thalamostriatal claim or a causal experimental perturbation.

The separate nonsignificant sNMDA (r=0.40,p=0.08), sGABA (r=0.29,p=0.21) and sigma_rule (r=-0.36,p=0.12) correlations apply specifically to the LEFT MIDDLE FRONTAL GYRUS cluster eigenvariate (Fig9A,C); no separate physiological-parameter nonsignificance for the thalamus/caudate ROI is shown. Combined model minimal action was used as the reported significant correlate.

The reduced 3D decision implementation sacrifices stability of high-activity decision attractors and invertible mapping of fitted effective decision parameters to physiological ones; no decision-module energy inference.

Source does not distinguish IFJ and IPS internal functional division; proposed maintenance-versus-representation allocations are speculative alternatives compatible with but not tested by this analysis.
Dopamine to AMPA/NMDA/GABA mechanisms are prior-grounded physiologically motivated explanatory proposals; this study did not directly perturb individual dopamine receptors in these participants.
Printed p33 tau_AMPA equality contradicts p30 Eq3 multiplication; use OU structural noise identity only, exclude exact numeric p33 normalization unless separate approved source confirms it.
claim_role_mapping.source_locator: PDF pp30,33; SHA-locked pre-A math adjudication

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: The white-noise diffusion and FP treatment approximates colored OU gating noise near its steady state; p37 Eq9 should not be presented as literal numerical equivalence for arbitrary transient times.

Human model fitted individual behavior; functional activation regressor is indirect boundary-relative trace, and microscopic synaptic parameters remain inferred through model rather than directly human-measured.

Behavioral simulation tests a fixed, pretrained network in baseline/distractor/switch only; does not reconstruct learning, the ambiguous high-uncertainty choice mechanism, or every human executive process.

PF02 is Stemme-2005-descended at integrated task-switch architecture level; relative central-family nonduplication with scoped #399 pilot slate is judged bounded, not globally independent historical novelty.

claim_role_mapping.source_claim: Behavioral correlations of fitted model rule-attractor depth with condition-specific reaction-time costs and errors in source Table2 yield no association surviving multiple-comparison correction. This cannot validate exact transient colored OU dynamics.
